- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.25), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.  
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or oscillating), model frequently overfits recent highs/lows; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period rallies (especially after sentiment shifts to positive); add 1–3% buffer for final 7–10 days if sentiment >0.6.  
- If sentiment history shows rapid reversal (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 or vice versa), model often misjudges direction; adjust forecast by 5–10% toward the sentiment trend’s new direction.
